text:
# Year 9 Lesson Plan: Causes of the First World War

## Class Context
- 34 students, mixed attainment (including 6 students with reading age <9)
- No student devices, projector available
- Printing budget: 1 A4 sheet per student

---

## Learning Objectives
By the end of the lesson, all students will be able to:
- **All:** Identify at least three long-term causes of WWI
- **Most:** Explain how the alliance system increased tension in Europe
- **Some:** Evaluate which cause was most significant and why

---

## Lesson Timeline

### **Starter: The Assassination Hook (5 minutes)**

| Time | Activity | Differentiation |
|------|----------|---------------|
| 0:00-5:00 | Project image of Franz Ferdinand's car in Sarajevo. Ask: "A man was shot in a small Balkan city. Six weeks later, all of Europe was at war. How?" Pair discussion, then brief whole-class response. | Visual hook supports lower literacy; open question allows all to contribute |

---

### **Main Part 1: The Powder Keg of Europe (15 minutes)**

| Time | Activity | Differentiation |
|------|----------|---------------|
| 5:00-12:00 | **Teacher exposition with projected diagram:** Draw and label "The Powder Keg" on whiteboard—explain how Europe was unstable before 1914. Introduce **M.A.N.I.A.** acronym as memory aid: **M**ilitarism, **A**lliances, **N**ationalism, **I**mperialism, **A**ssassination. Students copy into books. | Colour-code each factor on board; repeat acronym chorally; use physical gestures (marching for militarism, pointing for alliances) |
| 12:00-20:00 | **Picture analysis:** Project 5 images (one per factor): German soldiers marching, the Alliance map, Balkan nationalists, African colonial scramble, Sarajevo street. Students match to M.A.N.I.A. factors in books. Check answers with mini-whiteboards or thumbs up/down. | Paired discussion; sentence starters on board: "This shows..."; teaching assistant supports identified students |

---

### **Main Part 2: The Alliance System in Depth (15 minutes)**

| Time | Activity | Differentiation |
|------|----------|---------------|
| 20:00-25:00 | **Drama activity:** Allocate students to Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain). Use rope/string to show connections. Demonstrate: when Austria-Hungary pulls on Serbia (student), Russia pulls back, Germany supports Austria-Hungary, etc. | Kinaesthetic learning; physical demonstration of abstract concept; roles given verbally, not written |
| 25:00-30:00 | **Map completion:** Students use printed sheet (see below) to shade alliance members. Add arrows showing how one conflict became a world war. | Pre-shaded version available for 6 lowest-attaining students; peer support encouraged |
| 30:00-35:00 | **Source analysis:** Project simplified 1914 telegram: "Russia has mobilised. We must mobilise too. —Kaiser Wilhelm." Discuss: Why did Germany feel they *had* to act? | Read aloud; highlight key phrase; think-pair-share |

---

### **Main Part 3: Making Connections (10 minutes)**

| Time | Activity | Differentiation |
|------|----------|---------------|
| 35:00-42:00 | **Card sort (verbal/whole class):** Project 5 statements about causes. Students vote by moving to corners of room labelled: "Definitely a cause," "Partly a cause," "Not really a cause." Justify choices. Examples: "Germany wanted an empire," "The Kaiser had a withered arm," "France wanted revenge for 1871." | Movement engages all; no reading required for initial response; verbal reasoning developed |

---

### **Plenary: Understanding Check Before the Bell (8 minutes)**

| Time | Activity | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| 42:00-47:00 | **Exit ticket (verbal relay):** Students line up. Teacher asks each: "Name one long-term cause and one trigger of WWI." Correct answer = leave. Incorrect = step aside, discuss with TA/peer, retry. | **Checks understanding for every student**; immediate feedback; builds confidence |
| 47:00-50:00 | **Final consolidation:** Project M.A.N.I.A. with one question mark. "For homework: Which letter was most important? Be ready to argue tomorrow." Pack away. | Sets up next lesson; whole-class finish |

---

## The Single Printed Sheet (A4, double-sided)

### **Side 1: The Alliance Map of Europe, 1914**

```
[Simple outline map of Europe—countries labelled but not shaded]

SHADE AND LABEL:
□ Triple Alliance      □ Triple Entente      □ Neutral

GERMANY (colour RED)        FRANCE (colour BLUE)
AUSTRIA-HUNGARY (RED)       RUSSIA (BLUE)  
ITALY (RED)                 BRITAIN (BLUE)

DRAW ARROWS showing how the assassination in Serbia (1914) 
led to war across Europe.

Use this sentence to help:
"When Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, _______ 
supported Serbia because _______. Then _______ 
supported _______ because _______."
```

### **Side 2: M.A.N.I.A. Summary Table**

| Letter | Cause | Simple meaning | Example |
|--------|-------|---------------|---------|
| **M** | Militarism | Building up armies | Germany's navy scared Britain |
| **A** | Alliances | Promises to help other countries | Triple Alliance vs Triple Entente |
| **N** | Nationalism | Love of your country; wanting independence | Balkan peoples vs Austria-Hungary |
| **I** | Imperialism | Empire building | Scramble for Africa |
| **A** | Assassination | Murder for political reasons | Franz Ferdinand shot, 28 June 1914 |

**YOUR TURN:** Which cause was most important? Circle one and explain in one sentence below.

---

## Differentiation Summary

| Need | Strategy |
|------|----------|
| Reading age <9 | Pre-shaded maps; verbal questioning; TA support; paired work; physical activities |
| High attainers | Evaluation questions; lead roles in drama; peer teaching opportunities |
| EAL | Visuals, gestures, repeated key terms, sentence starters |

## Assessment for Learning

- **During lesson:** Thumbs up/down, mini-whiteboards (if available), observation of drama participation
- **Before bell:** Verbal exit ticket—**every student demonstrates understanding of at least one long-term cause and the trigger**
- **Written record:** Completed map and M.A.N.I.A. table in books
